brief: Tonight is Pull A — deadlift, wide pulldown, cable row, curls. Before any of that: you have written the same complaint into your log twice in four days and I kept prescribing over the top of it. You skipped the face pulls on Pull B on the 28th and wrote that running the same corrective on back-to-back days was insane. You were handed them again the next Push A and wrote three words. You were right and I was wrong, and the fix is a change to the plan, not a lecture to you. There are two cards waiting for you tonight: take face pulls off Pull A, and take them off Pull B. Say yes to both and they live on your two push days only, three days apart, never twice in a row. Tonight one of my trainers wanted to RAISE your face pulls to 29 because you topped the rep range on them last night. I threw that out. Two more answers I owe you. You asked why the calf raise had four sets — because I put a fourth one there on the 30th with an override, on a lift where you had already told me three, and I never said so. That was mine and it was wrong. You asked why the hanging leg raise came at you in seconds — because when I swapped it in for the plank it inherited the plank's stopwatch, and reps and seconds are not the same thing. That one is fixed in the app as of the 30th; if your card still says seconds tonight, your phone has an old copy and I need to know. And yes, I have your gym right now: the lat pulldown machine doubles as the cable row, one station, as you told me on the 24th. Now tonight. Nothing goes up in weight. The whole card is last Pull A's weights with a rep ask on top, because eight days ago every one of these landed on the floor of its range and the app was about to print that exact session back at you. Deadlift stays at 265 and I want six on all three top sets instead of five — you have made five every time and never once tried for six, and six is what buys 275. Wide pulldown: 135 for nine, then 150 for eight and eight; last time the third set fell to seven, so hold both eights and 157.5 is yours. Cable row: 105 for eleven, twelve, eleven — you have never taken twelve at 105, that is the ask. Dumbbell curls stay at the 30s for nine, nine, eight. Hammer curls 42.5 for eleven across, and I am reading that number as your two-hand rope version, which is what you told me you switched to on the 24th — if that is not what you are doing any more, write it on the lift like you did last time and I will rebuild its numbers from scratch. The one thing that will decide whether the sixth deadlift rep happens is rest, and your rest is not following the card — it follows one habit of about two minutes no matter what the lift is. Last Pull A the deadlift asked four minutes and you went again after two and a half, then three and a half, while the dumbbell curls asked seventy-five seconds and you took over two minutes on both. You are spending your rest on the curls and borrowing it from the heaviest thing in your week. The bell rings once on the deadlift; wait for it. Cutting the face pulls hands you back about four minutes, which is roughly what the deadlift is currently going without. Cardio: you have logged one session in eleven days, fifteen easy minutes on the 21st. Twenty to thirty easy minutes tomorrow, any machine.

flags.note: Face pulls: you were right. Two cards below take them off Pull A and Pull B, leaving them on your two push days only. One of my trainers wanted to raise them tonight; I overruled that.
Your calf raise had four sets on the 30th because I added a fourth with an override, on a lift where you had already told me three. That was my mistake, not the plan's.

Your rest is running about two minutes on everything. The deadlift asks four and got two and a half last Pull A, while the curls asked seventy-five seconds and got over two minutes. Same total time, spent on the wrong lifts.
No bodyweight logged since 206 lb on 21 July. Eleven days blind on the one number that tells me whether you are eating enough to recover from these deadlifts.

Close-grip pulldown is your one stalled lift — 120 for ten, ten, ten on both 21 and 28 July, stuck on the floor of its range. Nothing for you to decide: next Pull B I am asking 120 for twelve, eleven, eleven, and 127.5 the moment all three sets reach twelve.

dissent.progression: Raise to 29 for two sets of 14 — he took 27.5 for 15 and 15 on 2026-07-31, topping both sets of the 12-15 range, making this the only lift on the card that has actually earned a step.
dissent.recovery: Skip them entirely tonight — he did two sets last night, refused them in writing on 2026-07-28 and logged zero, and they buy nothing on back-to-back days.
dissent.why: Progression is right on the arithmetic and it does not matter. He topped the range on a lift he has told us twice, in writing, that he does not want on consecutive days — the reps went up because he did the work anyway, not because he wants more of it. Printing a raise on face pulls tonight, the morning after 'Do you have a brain?', would be the app answering a complaint with an increase. There is no override on this lift tonight and no weight is prescribed for it; the real answer is the two removal cards, which is a change to the program, which is where this belonged from the start. Progression loses nothing it can use — a rear-delt corrective is not what wins a March show.

dissent.progression: Hold 265 and ask for six reps on all three top sets — 5, 5, 5 is the floor of the 5-6 range and six is what earns 275.
dissent.recovery: Hold 265 and add nothing at all — he has taken the range floor twice running and never touched a six, and he hinged two days ago for 205 by nine and nine.
dissent.why: Both seats keep the bar at 265, so no weight is in dispute; the only question is whether I ask for the sixth rep. Recovery named no alternative number and its real argument is not fatigue — it is that his rest collapses on exactly this lift, two and a half minutes against a prescribed four. That is an argument for fixing the rest, not for asking less of him, and the brief and the flag both carry it. Cutting the face pulls, which I did on recovery's own call, hands back roughly the rest the deadlift is missing. Asking five when he has made five three times running is how a lift starts stalling on a card that says it is progressing.

proposals.why: You did face pulls on Push A last night and wrote "Do you have a brain?" next to them, and tonight's Pull A asks for them again — this drops them from Pull A only, so they stay on your two push days, where nothing else trains the back of the shoulder, and come off a day that already runs six sets of pulldowns and rows.

On Pull B you skipped the face pulls yourself and wrote that running the same corrective on back-to-back days was insane — this makes the plan say what you already did, leaving Pull B's thirteen other back sets to cover the rear delt and keeping face pulls on the two push days.

Pull A gives your biceps six direct sets and your only horizontal row three, and on 24 July all three row sets went at 105 for ten, eleven and ten with nothing falling off — this makes it four sets so the rowing on your back day at least matches the curling.

overrides.reason: Bar stays at 265 — you have made five on every top set you have ever done here and never tried for six. Six on all three is what buys 275. The bell rings once and it rings at four minutes; that rest is the whole reason the sixth rep is or is not there.
Same weights as last Pull A. Your third set fell to seven at 150, under the bottom of the range, so the job is two clean eights at 150 — hold those and 157.5 is yours. The opener goes to nine.
105 again. You went ten, eleven, ten last time and never touched the top of the range — twelve at 105 is a rep you have never done, and three of them moves you to 112.5.

The 30s stay. Last time was eight, eight, seven — that last set is under the range, and you took over two minutes rest on a lift that asks seventy-five seconds. Nine, nine, eight, and ten across earns the 35s.
42.5 across, read as your two-hand rope version. Ten, ten, ten last time is the floor of the range — eleven on all three is the ask, twelve across moves the pin.
